svg.title: RIEMANN · MAP T1 — The deepest chain: from a count of lattices by isometries up to the Riemann Hypothesis
svg.desc: One chain through the proof: 11 statements, each used by the proof of the next, from lem-local-lattice-counts-isometries at depth 10 up to thm-riemann-hypothesis of Main.lean. It is a shortest chain in the blueprint's uses graph, found breadth-first from the three theorems nothing else uses, so every statement on it is as far from the main theorems as it can be. Read it as a proof, left to right and top to bottom: nothing is used before it is proved. Each card is one blueprint statement, as in the chapter posters; an arrow from A to B says that the proof of B uses A. This is how deep the proof goes: no statement of the blueprint is farther from the main theorems than the first card. The chain runs through the families, the off-diagonal bound of the theta chapter, and down to a local lattice count. Map mode: nothing of the blueprint's text or the proof's source is quoted. No Lean was built: see diagram R1, band 5.

A ⇢ B: B is stated with A (dashed)

Title and pill. The title is the blueprint's; the pill gives the kind and the provenance: new in Alpöge's proof, modified from a published result, or published as it stands. Main.lean marks the theorems the

The line in italics gives the statement's id and how many paragraphs the blueprint spends on its statement and its proof. The text itself is not quoted: it is the blueprint's authors', and the blueprint link in the
footer has it. The Lean signature is not quoted either, for the same reason; the footer gives the declaration's name, file and line in the mirror.
Stated with, Proof uses and Used by are the blueprint's edges, in full. An arrow from A to B: the proof of B uses A, and the arrow takes A's colour.

The chain, in reading order: 1. lem-local-lattice-counts-isometries (Theta lifts, periods and the Siegel-Weil formula, depth 10); 2. lem-local-partner-counts (Theta lifts, periods and the Siegel-Weil formula, depth 9); 3. prop-pair-coefficient-local-decomposition (Theta lifts, periods and the

The chapters it crosses, in order: chap-theta → chap-families → architecture → main-theorems.
Depth counts uses edges from the main theorems: lem-local-lattice-counts-isometries is at depth 10, the deepest statement on the chain. The blueprint's deepest statement of all is at depth 10.
